test_title: PYST 59: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A woman using a copper-T complains of abdominal pain and discomfort. What is the likely reason?

options.text: Uterine irritation caused by the IUD

solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterine irritation caused by the IUD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Copper-T** is a type of **Intrauterine Device (IUD)** that is inserted into the **uterus** to prevent pregnancy. Because it is a **foreign object**, the body may react to its presence, leading to **uterine irritation** and subsequent **abdominal discomfort**.
 
• When an **IUD** is inserted, it can cause the **uterine muscles** to contract or cramp as they adjust to the device. This physical **irritation** of the **endometrium** (uterine lining) is the most common cause of localized pain. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Infection in the stomach** is usually caused by **bacteria** or **viruses** ingested through food or water and is physiologically unrelated to the placement of a contraceptive device in the **reproductive tract**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Copper-T** is a **non-hormonal** contraceptive method. It works through the release of **copper ions** rather than chemicals like **estrogen** or **progesterone** found in **tablets**; therefore, it does not cause **hormonal imbalance** associated with oral pills. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• While certain **infections** (like PID) can lead to complications, a **blockage in the fallopian tube** is generally a cause of **infertility** and does not typically manifest as immediate abdominal discomfort specifically triggered by the presence of a **Copper-T**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Copper-T:**
 
 
• The **Copper-T** releases **copper ions** into the **uterine cavity**, which act as a **spermicide**. This environment is toxic to **sperm**, preventing **fertilization** by inhibiting sperm motility.
 
• It also causes a **local inflammatory response** in the **uterus**, which prevents a fertilized egg from **implanting** in the uterine wall.
 
 
 
• **Types of IUDs:**
 
 
• **Non-Hormonal IUDs:** Includes the **Copper-T (CuT-380A)**, which can remain effective for up to **10 years**.
 
• **Hormonal IUDs:** Devices like **Mirena** or **Levonorgestrel**-releasing systems (LNG-IUS) release **progestin** to thicken **cervical mucus** and thin the **uterine lining**.
 
 
 
• **Side Effects:**
 
 
• Common side effects of the **Copper-T** include **menorrhagia** (heavy menstrual bleeding) and **dysmenorrhea** (painful periods), especially during the first **3 to 6 months** after **insertion**.
 
• **Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)** is a rare risk, usually occurring shortly after insertion if **bacteria** are introduced into the **reproductive tract**.
 
 
 
• **Application and Usage:**
 
 
• **IUDs** are classified as **Long-Acting Reversible Contraceptives (LARC)**. They are highly effective with a **failure rate** of less than **1%**.
 
• The **insertion** must be performed by a trained **healthcare professional** or **doctor** to ensure the device is placed correctly within the **fundus** of the **uterus**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ideal Candidates:** **IUDs** are often recommended for women who desire long-term **birth control** and want to avoid daily **tablets** or **hormonal** side effects.
 
• **Post-Insertion Care:** Patients are advised to check the **IUD strings** regularly to ensure the device has not been **expelled**, which occurs in about **2% to 10%** of users.
 
• **Contraindications:** Women with **unexplained vaginal bleeding**, **uterine fibroids** that distort the cavity, or active **pelvic infections** should avoid using a **Copper-T**.
</ul
